headline: Fear persists as Fed enters blackout under political crossfire
body: With US markets closed for Labor Day, sentiment is still anchored to Friday's session and the data that drove it: a much stronger-than-expected August jobs report — payrolls up 162,000 against a roughly 53,000 estimate, unemployment steady at 4.1% — sent the S&P 500 down 0.38% to 7,718.60, the Nasdaq off 0.29%, and the Dow down 0.51%. The beat flipped the prevailing rate story, pushing hike-odds estimates for the September 16-18 meeting into a wide band from roughly a coin flip to the mid-60s across different prediction markets, versus near 33% only weeks ago. Oil has eased slightly from Wednesday's spike after Iran's strikes on Gulf bases but Brent and WTI remain elevated, keeping a geopolitical premium in the mix. The Fear & Greed Index sits at 42 — Fear, but up from deeper readings.

Layered on top is an unusually direct political pressure campaign: President Trump has threatened new tariffs on trade-deficit countries if the Fed doesn't cut rates, and Vice President Vance has separately pushed for lower rates to ease housing costs — all landing just as the Fed enters its pre-meeting quiet period through September 17. Underneath the macro and political noise, the AI trade remains the market's structural narrative, with the Nasdaq-100 having just completed another AI-infrastructure-heavy rebalance even as the index carries a historically weak September seasonal pattern. Searches for retail chatter today turned up tracking tools rather than a distinct, coordinated mood, so this read leans more on the jobs-data surprise, Fed-pressure headlines, and lingering oil risk than on any clear social-sentiment signal.
